questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Iceland?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Towns and cities” part of the Iceland article.

questions.proof: Reykjavík is the capital city of Iceland.

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of Iceland?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “People” part of the Iceland article.

questions.proof: The language they speak is Icelandic.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “Iceland is north of Ireland, east of Greenland, west of _____, northwest of the United Kingdom, east of Canada, and southwest of Svalbard and Jan Mayen.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “northwest”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Iceland article.

questions.proof: Iceland is an island country between the North Atlantic and Arctic, between Greenland and Norway.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “Iceland is 301 kilometers east of Greenland and _____ kilometers west of Norway.”

hints.nudge: It is a year in the eleventh century.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Iceland article.

questions.proof: Iceland is 301 kilometers east of Greenland and 1001 kilometers west of Norway.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “When _____ took over Denmark on April 9 1940, the Althing decided that Icelanders should rule the country themselves, but they did not declare independence yet.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “took”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: It is further down the Iceland article, under the heading “History”.

questions.proof: When Germany took over Denmark on April 9 1940, the Althing decided that Icelanders should rule the country themselves, but they did not declare independence yet.
